thread:
maya: Quick thread — observed a ~18% p50 latency regression on SM90 when our selector switched from flash_v2 -> paged_hybrid for an 8k longseq nightly canary. Repro steps + logs below. cc @cheng @noah :eyes:
cheng: Can you paste the selector config and raw numbers? Also which CUDA/Triton stack? I remember some FP16 kernel diffs on CUDA 12.2.
maya: Selector snippet:
```json
{
  "seq_len": 8192,
  "preferred": ["paged_hybrid", "flash_v2"],
  "kv_policy": "prefetch",
  "batching": {"max_batch_size": 32, "microbatch_ms": 4}
}
```
Numbers we saw (nightly canary, minimal load):
- flash_v2: p50 = 42ms, p95 = 110ms, kv_hit ~0.95
- paged_hybrid: p50 = 50ms, p95 = 132ms, kv_hit ~0.78
Environment: SM90 (A100S), CUDA 12.2, Triton 2.17, model: gpt-3.5-medium.
noah: Did you capture nsight or pprof? Any L2/DRAM breakdowns? Paged variants can do more DRAM IO if the KV layout causes extra page walks.
maya: I uploaded a perf dump (pprof + nvtx) -> http://perf.local/pprof/1967890123. KV log snippet shows eviction spikes around token boundary ~2048. Hit ratio drops right before p95 spikes.
diego: Quick hypothesis: prefetch policy + paged layout is thrashing the KV cache leading to more global loads; flash_v2 keeps more contiguous memory locality.
sylvia: Two concrete levers to test: (1) force cache_mode=sticky (prevent eviction) and (2) disable kv_prefetch (so we don't prefetch pages we won't use). Also isolate Triton vs native CUDA kernels to see kernel-level perf.
cheng: I ran a small microbench yesterday comparing triton vs cuda kernels on sm90 for an attention microkernel — difference was ~5% in isolation. 18% smells like cache/memory behavior. If Triton is hitting a fallback path for some heads that could amplify perf diff.
maya: Repro command we used:
```
./bench_longseq --model gpt-3.5-medium --seq 8192 --batch 8 --arch sm90 --kernel paged_hybrid --runs 50
```
Attached nvprof timeline shows repeated device->device stalls at token offsets where eviction happens.
diego: Running canaries now: 4 permutations
- flash_v2 (control)
- paged_hybrid (default)
- paged_hybrid + cache_mode=sticky
- paged_hybrid + cache_mode=sticky + kv_prefetch=0
Also will try CUDA 12.1 vs 12.2 to rule toolchain regressions. Will post numbers in ~25m. :coffee:
perf-bot: diego started job canary/196789-run1 (sm90, paged_hybrid) -- ETA ~20m
diego: Results: (node A100S, identical load)
- flash_v2: p50=43ms p95=118ms kv_hit=0.95
- paged_hybrid (default): p50=51ms p95=134ms kv_hit=0.78
- paged_hybrid + sticky: p50=45ms p95=120ms kv_hit=0.93
- paged_hybrid + sticky + kv_prefetch=0: p50=44ms p95=119ms kv_hit=0.94
Also tried CUDA 12.1 vs 12.2: with sticky set the numbers converge (delta < 2%). Without sticky, both toolchains show the regression.
noah: That strongly indicates the perf delta is due to eviction/prefetch interaction rather than a fundamental kernel inefficiency on SM90. Actionable items:
- Selector heuristic: prefer sticky cache when picking paged_hybrid for seq_len >= 6k.
- Add runtime KPI: if kv_hit < 0.85 for rolling 5m + p50 increase > 10% -> auto-fallback to flash_v2 for that route.
- Add a CI microtest that runs paged_hybrid on SM90 for seq=8k and asserts p50 within 10% of flash_v2 (so we catch regressions in premerge).
maya: I'll file an RFC and tickets: selector tweak + canary KPI + perf CI test. Draft RFC: https://go/rfcs/2026-selector-paged-hybrid (WIP). I'll also add the pprof pointers to the ticket.
sylvia: Also add a short note in the model onboarding checklist: when enabling paged variants, verify kv_policy and cache_mode on SM90 for longseq workloads.
diego: I'll roll a small config change to the selector to prefer sticky for paged_hybrid in canary, and run a week of canaries before wider rollout.
maya: Awesome — thanks all. TL;DR: regression root cause = eviction + prefetch interplay; mitigation = selector heuristics + sticky cache + canary KPI + CI test. :thumbsup:
cheng: Nice triage. If we re-run with a larger batch or different microbatch_ms we should also check per-GPU occupancy, but that's secondary now.
noah: Filing two tickets: PERF-3721 (selector heuristic) and PERF-3722 (canary KPI + auto-fallback).
perf-bot: Created PERF-3721, PERF-3722, assigned to maya/diego.
maya: Will follow up with PRs and link them here. Thanks!
